description: Technical design document with implementation details
instruction:
Create the design document that explains HOW to implement the change.

When to include design.md (create only if any apply):
- Cross-cutting change (multiple services/modules) or new architectural pattern
- New external dependency or significant data model changes
- Security, performance, or migration complexity
- Ambiguity that benefits from technical decisions before coding

Sections:
- **Context**: Only the current state and constraints needed to explain the approach. Reference the proposal for motivation instead of restating it (e.g., "See proposal.md - Why").
- **Goals / Non-Goals**: What this design achieves and explicitly excludes. Don't restate the proposal's scope - add only design-level boundaries.
- **Decisions**: Key technical choices with rationale (why X over Y?). Include alternatives considered for each decision.
- **Risks / Trade-offs**: Known limitations, things that could go wrong. Format: [Risk] → Mitigation
- **Migration Plan**: Steps to deploy, rollback strategy (if applicable)
- **Open Questions**: Unknowns that can safely be answered later without
  changing the specs, the approach, or the task breakdown. Omit if none.

Open questions are for genuinely deferrable unknowns, not decisions you
skipped. If a question would change the specs, the chosen approach, or
the task breakdown, resolve it now - ask the user instead of guessing.

Focus on architecture and approach, not line-by-line implementation.
The proposal covers why and what; design covers how. Reference the
proposal for motivation and, once written, the specs for requirements -
if a section would only restate them, point to them instead.

Good design docs explain the "why" behind technical decisions.
context:
# Product

A Data Room: one authenticated owner, one Data Room, an arbitrarily deep tree of folders and
files inside it, shared read-only (public link or named grantee) and revocably. Built as a
take-home, graded in this order: (1) UX and functionality, (2) design and polish, (3) code
quality. "Don't include unimplemented features" is part of the grading.

# Spec source of truth

`docs/` is the plan. Cite its stable IDs (`FR-<AREA>-<nnn>`, `BR-<nnn>`) in every artifact.

- `docs/01-scope.md` — tiers (Core / Polish / Extra credit), what was cut, traceability to the brief
- `docs/02-requirements.md` — authority for requirements, rules and limits
- `docs/03-domain-and-api.md` — authority for field names, endpoints, error codes, storage,
  the environment contract and the scaling answers
- `docs/04-ux.md` — screens, interactions, component inventory, state ownership
- `docs/05-build-order.md` — slices; one OpenSpec change is normally one slice

Retired IDs, never reused: FR-SRCH-030, FR-SRCH-040, FR-SRCH-050, BR-090 (semantic search, cut).

# Repository

pnpm + Turborepo. From the root: `pnpm dev`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck`,
`pnpm lint`; scope with `--filter @dataroom/api` or `@dataroom/web`.

- `apps/api` — NestJS 11, routes under `/api` (`API_PREFIX` from the shared package), global
  `ValidationPipe` (`whitelist`, `forbidNonWhitelisted`), Jest. Planned: Prisma + Postgres,
  Passport JWT, `@aws-sdk/client-s3`.
- `apps/web` — Vite 8 + React 19, Vitest. Planned: Tailwind v4 + shadcn/ui (copied into
  `src/components/ui/`), TanStack Router + Query, Zustand, `XMLHttpRequest` for upload progress.
- `packages/shared` — `@dataroom/shared`, compiles to CJS so Nest can require it. Every type that
  crosses the API/web boundary lives here and is never duplicated in an app.
- Blobs: one private S3-compatible bucket — MinIO via `docker compose` locally, any S3-compatible
  store elsewhere, one code path.
- Hosting: none is chosen, and none is named in the code. The app runs locally and is deployed by
  whoever wants it, wherever they want it (see `docs/03` § Running it somewhere else). The only
  constraint the code imposes: the API needs a persistent process, because uploads stream through
  Nest. `DATABASE_URL` at runtime, `DIRECT_URL` for `prisma migrate deploy`.

# Domain model

`User` → `DataRoom` (one per user today; the model allows several) → `Node` rows. One table does
folders and files: a folder is a node with no blob, a file is a node with one. `Share` rows grant
read-only access to one node and its whole subtree. `dataRoomId` is the scope column and leads
every index.

# Invariants — do not break one without an explicit decision from the user

- BR-010 — every request resolves to one principal: owner (JWT) or share (token). Scope is checked
  once per request against the Data Room. A node the principal has no claim on returns
  `404 NOT_FOUND`, never `403`.
- BR-020 — names are unique per `(dataRoomId, parentId)`, case-insensitive; a conflict appends
  ` (2)` before the extension and the response carries the name actually used. One shared helper —
  never a second implementation for move, copy or upload.
- BR-030 — every delete confirms first and states the real recursive counts from
  `GET /nodes/:id/stats`, never "and its contents".
- BR-040 — uploads are validated server-side on sniffed MIME type and size before any blob is
  written. SVG is not in the allow list.
- BR-050 — every failure is visible; uploads retry twice on a network error or 5xx and never on a
  4xx; a failed upload leaves no row and no orphan blob.
- BR-060 — blob first, row second, failed row write deletes the blob; subtree delete/move/copy run
  in one transaction.
- BR-070 — handlers ask the principal for a capability (`read` / `write`), never for the header, the
  token or the role name. `Share.role` exists and only holds `VIEWER` today.
- BR-100 — nothing ships disabled or half-implemented: remove it from the UI instead. And nothing
  is wired to one machine — no host, port, origin or bucket name is hardcoded; each is an env var
  with a local default, listed in `docs/03` § Configuration.

# Conventions

- The server enforces. Hiding a button is not access control.
- One error envelope `{ code, message, details? }` from a global exception filter; codes come from
  `docs/03-domain-and-api.md`.
- Listings are keyset-paginated on `(type, name, id)`, default 100 rows, and never show total counts.
- `BigInt` is converted to `number` once, in the serialisation layer.
- Tier discipline: a Core change never pulls in Polish or Extra-credit work. If it seems to need
  to, say so in the proposal.
- Capability paths under `openspec/specs/` mirror the requirement areas in `docs/02`: `auth`,
  `data-room`, `navigation`, `folders`, `files`, `viewing`, `sharing`, `search`, `versioning`,
  `ui-shell`, and `platform/{persistence,http,authz,delivery,testing}`.

# Validation scripts — mandatory, one per change

Every change ships `scripts/validate/<change-name>.sh` and is not complete until it exits 0.
Jest and Vitest prove the code in isolation; this script proves the change against the app that is
actually running — real Postgres, real MinIO, real HTTP — which is what the archive gate means by
"verified by hand". Writing it is a task in `tasks.md`, not an afterthought. Its contract:

- Bash, `set -euo pipefail`, executable, no required arguments.
- Hosts come from the environment with a local default — `API_BASE_URL`
  (`http://localhost:3000/api`), `WEB_BASE_URL` (`http://localhost:5173`) — never hardcoded
  (BR-100). An unreachable API prints the URL tried and exits non-zero, never skips (BR-050).
- It creates the accounts, folders and files it needs through the public API and deletes them at
  the end, so two consecutive runs both pass and it never leans on another script's leftovers.
- One assertion per scenario, each line naming the `FR-*`/`BR-*` ID it proves and pass/fail. A
  failure prints the request plus expected versus actual status and error code, then exits
  non-zero on the spot.
- Failure paths are the point: assert the `404`/`409`/`413`/`415` the change introduces, not only
  the happy path.
- It ends by printing the manual checklist for what only a browser can show (focus, drag-drop,
  optimistic UI), so hand-verification before archive is a list, not a memory exercise.
- Dropping the script needs an explicit decision from the user, recorded in `design.md`.
rules: Self-contained. Copy the concrete field names, endpoint signatures, error codes, index names and env vars out of docs/03 into this file. "See docs/03" is a context miss: the apply step does not read docs/.
State which BR-* invariants the change touches and how it upholds each one.
Name the one alternative that was rejected, and why.
List the FR/BR IDs the validation script proves at runtime, and the ones it cannot — those become the manual checklist it prints.
